opened: Spindle is a GPU compute network design built on Robinhood Chain. Providers register GPU nodes and serve AI jobs in a sealed or open lane. Each job emits a signed receipt and verified earnings accrue in USDG. The payout design offers USDG, canonical Stock Tokens or a virtual card, with split claims supported. This site presents the v1.1 specification and an illustrative dashboard; it does not display live earnings or guarantee demand.

opened: Which GPUs and APIs are supported?

The specification includes sealed-lane confidential GPUs such as H100, H200 and B200-class hardware, alongside an open lane for non-sensitive work on suitable consumer GPUs. The API design supports chat completions, embeddings and images. The node agent benchmarks each GPU and detects its available lane; production access details are coming soon.

Hourly cumulative Merkle roots support provider claims. A receipt evidences work on the measured stack; it does not prove the AI output was correct.

opened: Only the sealed lane is designed to keep prompts private from the operator. It requires eligible confidential GPUs, a TDX environment and current attestation, with OHTTP for the request path. Open-lane jobs are not confidential. The specification discloses TEE limits and does not establish a SOC 2 audit.

opened: How do the payout routes work?

Verified earnings accrue in USDG. The claim design offers a USDG wallet transfer, a quote for a canonical Stock Token, or a virtual card through a third-party program. Split claims share the same cumulative entitlement. Card regions and terms, as well as Stock Token liquidity and issuer eligibility, determine which route is available.

The agent benchmarks the GPU, detects confidential-compute support, creates a node key and registers through a passkey smart account on Robinhood Chain. The website is a specification preview; it does not promise a setup time or provide live node enrollment.

tree: For every role in the compute network
One network for compute, receipts and payout choice
Spindle connects GPU providers with AI workloads. Jobs leave signed receipts, verified earnings accrue in USDG, and providers choose how to route a claim.

v: How does a job reach a payout route?
How does a job reach a payout route?

tree: Spindle connects the steps from GPU to payout
and leaves the route choice with you.

c: Each completed job carries a signed receipt, with metering checked before it reaches the ledger.
Sealed jobs (in testing) need confidential GPUs and attestation. Open jobs are non-sensitive workloads.
The claim design shows the route, quote and applicable conditions before a provider signs a claim.

tree: Everything between the AI request and the provider claim
The node signs a COSE receipt for each job. Verification checks its signature, job billing and measured units before the work enters the USDG earnings ledger.
The dashboard design brings node state, compute lane, receipt epochs and claim routes into one view. Preview records illustrate the flow; they are not live network metrics.
A defined path from job to claim
Verified receipts feed the earnings ledger. An hourly root records cumulative entitlement, then the provider chooses the claim route and signs the request.
